en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is renowned for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical cone shapes of any volcano in the world.
The tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, is one of the rarest and most endangered mammals in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley region.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique lake located within a volcanic crater, which itself is situated on a larger lake.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
Siargao Island in Surigao del Norte is widely known as the surfing capital of the Philippines due to its famous Cloud 9 break.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and one of the largest and rarest eagles in the world.
Baguio City in the Cordillera region experiences a subtropical highland climate, making it significantly cooler than the rest of the tropical Philippines.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling chocolate kisses.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in Zambales was the second-largest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century, significantly cooling global temperatures.
